simple.meaning: מֶלְקָח (melqâch) is a Hebrew object word meaning “(only in dual) tweezers.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 25:38. The surrounding context includes altar.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מֶלְקָח (H4457) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מֶלְקָח (melqâch) / H4457 is traced through Exodus 25:38, Exodus 37:23, Numbers 4:9, 1 Kings 7:49 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Its snuffers and its snuff dishes shall be of pure gold.

timeline.evidenceText: Its snuffers and its snuff dishes shall be of pure gold.
He made its seven lamps, and its snuffers, and its snuff dishes, of pure gold.

and the flowers, the lamps, and the tongs of gold that was perfect gold;

definitions.full: H4457. melqach or malqach מֶלְקָחַ֫יִם , [ מַלְקָחַיִם ] noun [masculine] dual tongs, snuffers ; — 1 tongs used at altar of temple , for lifting coal, in Isaiah's vision, Isa 6:6 . 2 lamp snuffers , in temple 1Kin 7:49 2Chr 4:21 ; in tabernacle suffix ( reference to lamp-stand, מְנוֺרָה ) מַלְקָחֶיהָ Exod 25:38 ; 37:23 ; Num 4:9 (all P).
